root_cause: The protected Portal API contract and production data path were separately proven, but the release chain had no durable way to create a real short-lived authenticated Netlify Identity session from CI. That left authenticated HTTP 200 against /api/portal-ondernemersdata as a manual/session-dependent evidence gap.
fix: Production Release Readback now obtains a short-lived GitHub Actions OIDC token restricted to this repository, main and the production readback workflow. A Netlify-only canary endpoint verifies its signature and claims, creates an auto-confirmed ephemeral Identity user with a synthetic tenant, performs server-side login, returns only the session cookie, and deletes the canary after the normal protected endpoint returns HTTP 200 with the same tenant scope.
prevention: Protected Portal APIs that are part of production readiness must have a real authenticated HTTP readback, not only unit tests plus database/provider proof.
CI authentication must use short-lived federated identity where possible; do not store permanent customer credentials for canaries.
GitHub OIDC subject validation must account for the repository's legacy and immutable owner/repository-ID subject formats while still requiring the same repository, main ref and workflow claims.
A production canary must exercise the unchanged customer auth boundary and must never introduce a canary header or alternate authentication path inside the business API.
Canary users and credentials are ephemeral and removed after readback, including failure cleanup.

evidence.production_claim: withheld until protected merge, exact-main Netlify deployment and authenticated HTTP 200 artifact

delivery_recovery.root_cause: The initial PR description used narrative headings but omitted the repository's exact machine-readable delivery metadata preamble, so admission correctly failed before expensive CI.
delivery_recovery.fix: Write Obligation-ID, Delivery-Lane, Candidate-Type, Base-SHA, Supersedes, Change-Scope and Scope-Budget as the first PR-body fields before triggering Required.
delivery_recovery.prevention: Every future candidate in this lineage must preserve the exact machine metadata preamble; narrative sections are supplementary, never a substitute.
